rules: R1: Breaking implies actionable: a project whose existing code fails or behaves differently has something to change (pin, adapt, or opt back), matching every agreed breaking record.

R2: Reverts are judged as behaviour changes against the immediately previous version; they are breaking when they change something application code observes (ASGI events received, client address, request context), not fixes, unless the record calls them a fix.

R3: Breaking = semantic change to what existing code receives on existing input/config without opt-in (accept/reject, parse output, client address, events, context, required dependencies). Not breaking: diagnostic/log/help/traceback display changes, and semantically equivalent output representation changes.

R4: A change the source itself labels a fix or a correction ("fix(...)", "more accurately", "more consistently", "preserve", completing a protocol handshake, honouring a disabled setting) is change_type fix, not breaking (fix restoring intended behaviour), benefit correctness - unless it is type-only.
R5: Type-only changes (inferred types, parameter typing) get benefit none per BENEFIT_RULE; a type correction is change_type fix.

R6: Benefits only when stated: capabilities ("allows applications to detect", "near-zero-downtime", "reducing dependency conflicts", sendBeacon preference, re-translation) get none; correctness only when the record states the old result was wrong (overflow, wrongly rejected keys, lost data); security only when a vulnerability/attack/bypass is named; performance only when speed/resource savings are claimed.
R7: Stricter validation listed as a deliberate breaking change (agreed breaking=true) is behavior_change, not fix, for consistency with the fix=not-breaking rule.

R8: Console warnings, debug-mode messages and SDK debug flags are change_type other (as agreed for the $sdk_debug_* and session-diagnostic records); changes to captured event/product data are behavior_change.

R9: Broadening the values an existing option accepts (null bootstrap, case-insensitive log_level, os.PathLike) is new_option and actionable; making existing options/defaults take effect at run time in another implementation (ws_ping_* in wsproto, like keepalive pings in websockets-sansio) or adding values to data the runtime already provides (scope["server"], like os.name in logs) is behavior_change and not actionable.
R10: Something that existed being dropped ("Drop iso time") is removal.
R11: Default changes that only alter displayed output (traceback locals, typo suggestions) are not breaking and not actionable, matching agreed default_change records.
R12: A new contract on values the project reads (false vs undefined feature flag results) is actionable: calling code must interpret the distinction.
